scenario: Autonomous ice-shelf basal sensors only transmit melt-rate observations exceeding 3.5 m/yr (satellite-resolution floor). Transmitted observations show a mean of 5.1 m/yr (σ=0.9 m/yr). Glaciologists want the true mean basal melt rate across all ice-shelf positions.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming basal melt rate follows a normal distribution with σ=0.9 m/yr, solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 3.5] = 5.1. (b) What fraction of all basal melt rate events lie above the 3.5 m/yr threshold? (c) By how much (in m/yr) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 5.1 m/yr is E[X|X>3.5], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=5.1 numerically yields μ=5.00733 m/yr. Only 95.3% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 0.09267 m/yr. Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean basal melt rate is 5.1 m/yr because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 3.5 m/yr are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>3.5], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=3.5, σ=0.9. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 5.1 and solve for μ via brentq on [-19.0, 5.0999]. (4) Solution: μ=5.00733 m/yr. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((3.5−5.00733)/0.9)=0.95301.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 5.1,0.9,3.5
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-5.00733)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.95301)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-0.09267)<0.01
